newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. utility restructuring consideration delayed.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. utility restructuring consideration delayed.

text.p: The New York Public Service Commission said Tuesday it has delayed for two months consideration of restructuring settlement agreements filed by four New York electric utilities.

Regulators had previously said they expected a decision on Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc's settlement in June followed by considerations of the proposals from Orange and Rockland Utilities, Central Hudson Gas and Electric and Rochester Gas and Electric. The
proposals are now expected to come to regulators for consideration in August and September, the commission said.

The delay resulted from the commission's decision to grant a motion by New York Attorney General Dennis Vacco requesting a recommended decision be issued on the proposed Con Edison rate and restructuring agreement, the commission said in a statement.
This means the case will be heard by an administrative law judge, who will issue the recommended decision, commission spokesman David Flanagan said.

Based on the commission decision Tuesday, the statement said, "once a recommended decision is issued publicly, the active parties in the case will have 20 days to submit briefs on exceptions and 15 days to submit briefs opposing exceptions. As a result ... it is anticiapted that the four proposed settlements will come to the commission for consideration in August and September."

Flanagan said there is no schedule for law judge consideration of each case and suggested that one could work back from the planned August and September consideration by the full commission to determine when the law judges would become involved.
He said there was no mention at Tuesday's commission meeting of the letter granting Con Edison authority to begin accounting for revenues on April 1 as though the settlement were already in effect.
This was implemented because Con Edison had been scheduled to put rate increases into effect April 1 which it gave up under settlement, Flanagan explained.
A spokesman said Con Edison expects discussions with the commission which will allow the new accounting remain in place subject to refund if changes are made.
